column2: Given these definitions: (1) Repentance is a compound of separable elements, such as sorrow, resolve to amend, and the facing of what one did, so it can contain the contrary of a condition without being identical to that contrary. (2) Repentance is the turning toward the grace that freely gives a maker the standing toward his own work. (3) To stand turned toward something is to hold a turning toward it as a standing over time, which persists without continuous attention to it. Then repentance contains sin's contrary, the standing turned toward one's own work, only once it comes to that standing.
